office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Two Democrats: one-term Rep. Lisa Parshley, a veterinary oncologist and former Olympia councilmember, faces first-time candidate Jamie Keenan-deVargas, a renter and immigrant-rights organizer who refuses corporate money and runs to her left on rent caps, single-payer health care and criminal justice.

candidates.summary: One-term state representative and former Olympia councilmember, a veterinary oncologist, running on affordability, housing supply, renter protections and health care.
highlights: Prime sponsor of HB 1445, the Washington health trust bill for universal public coverage [S15]
Voted for ESSB 6346 and says she 'fought and voted for the Millionaires' Tax' [S3][S6]
Voted for 2025 rent stabilization and supports building 'more homes of every type' [S2][S10]
Voted for ESHB 1296; opposes I-1 and I-638 [S7][S20]
Top contributors include Regence, Genentech, Puget Sound Energy and DaVita [S22]

taxes.basis: Yes on ESSB 6346 and ESSB 5813, says she fought for the millionaires tax, and sponsors a health-insurer premium tax increase.

spending.basis: Pushes expanded childcare subsidies and dedicated affordable-housing funding; voted for the 2025-27 operating budget.

housing.basis: Pairs supply-first 'more homes of every type' with stronger renter protections, a rent-stabilization vote and affordable-housing funding bills.

climate.basis: Voted for clean fuels program changes; endorsed by Washington Conservation Action and Sierra Club.

experience.basis: One House term plus six years on the Olympia City Council, against a first-time candidate.

reform.basis: Accepts contributions of $2,200 to $2,400 from companies and PACs (Regence, Genentech, PSE and Proliance Surgeons PAC at $2,400; DaVita at $2,200).

immigration.basis: Voted for 2SHB 2105 (immigrant worker protections) and SSB 5855 (limits on law-enforcement face coverings).

healthcare.basis: Prime sponsor of the Washington health trust (universal coverage) bill, member of the Universal Health Care Commission.

social.basis: Prime sponsor of an abortion savings program bill, endorsed by Planned Parenthood Votes NW, opposes I-638.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296 and against Republican amendments to it; opposes I-1.

tech.basis: Sponsors bargaining over AI use by public employers; voted for the data-center energy bill E2SHB 2515.

candidates.summary: Retail worker, renter and founder of immigrant-defense groups running for office for the first time on a volunteer-led, corporate-PAC-free campaign.
highlights: Rejects corporate PAC and lobbying money; top priority is restricting corporate political spending [S2][S5]
Supports inflation-capped rents, repeal of the local rent-control ban and state social housing [S2]
Supports single-payer health care, free childcare and new wealth taxes such as a 2% tax on financial intangibles [S2][S5]
Calls for decriminalizing drug use and removing school resource officers [S4][S5]

taxes.basis: Platform 'heavily reliant on tax restructuring': intangibles tax on $100M+ portfolios, land value tax, windfall-profits tax.

spending.basis: Proposes free childcare, single-payer health care, fare-free transit and state social housing.

housing.basis: Statewide rent caps at inflation, repeal of the rent-control ban, social housing, Housing First and right to counsel.

safety.basis: Divest from prisons, unarmed co-responders, full drug decriminalization, remove school resource officers.

climate.basis: Wants a zero-emission framework and state codification of federal standards, but calls carbon taxes regressive.

experience.basis: First run for office; runs explicitly against 'career politicians'.

local-control.basis: Says state preemption on zoning 'must be massively expanded', while also wanting local authority over rent control restored.

reform.basis: Rejects corporate PAC and lobbying money; proposes corporate political-spending limits and public election vouchers.

immigration.basis: Founded two immigrant-defense groups; wants immigration incarceration abolished and ICE legislated out of Washington.

healthcare.basis: Supports single-payer and the Washington Health Trust 'unequivocally'.

social.basis: Opposes I-638; endorsed by Washington State Stonewall Democrats; no other stated position.

parental-rights.basis: Listed as opposing I-1; no other statement on notification or opt-outs.

tech.basis: Would ban AI rent-pricing software and private police surveillance and impose strict data-center mandates.
